what: A substitution that reverts --select-cell's focus to "only creatures of ownership" — the exact defect Issue #373 opened about — has to redden criterion 2's check on (16,7). It does. This file also records a real regression this exercise caught in an earlier draft of the fix itself, and how it was found and corrected before this commit.

mutant.appliedOnTopOf: the committed, regression-fixed ApplySelectCellArgument (see regressionFoundAndFixed below), built, run and reverted without ever being committed itself

before.note: The fixed code, evidence/373-focus.json's criterion2 block.
before.controlFeedback: (16,7): 1 of 2 standing here; click the cell again for the next one.

after.controlFeedback: Pick a brush, then drag a rectangle on the map: the whole area is marked by one command. Esc cancels a drag, then puts the brush away.
after.reading: Mutated, the cell holds zero bodies under ApplySelectCellArgument's creature-only filter, so WorldLabels.SelectionHint(state, cell, chosen=null) short-circuits on selected being null and never fires — _controlFeedback is left exactly as it was before any cell was named, the plain brush-picker sentence. That untouched sentence, standing where "(16,7): 1 of 2 standing here..." stood in the fixed run, is what the mutant reddens.

reddened.what: Criterion 2 ("the frame with the raider under focus") is exactly what this mutant breaks: --select-cell 16,7 no longer reports two raiders standing there, although two do, reproducing verbatim the failure Issue #373 measured on the pre-fix codebase ("--select-cell не дотягивается вовсе... заполняет _selectedCreatureId только из state.Creatures").
reddened.howNotJustAsserted: Both runs print the identical canonical checksum, so the mutant is presentation-only — it could not have been caught by any Simulation-layer test. The bottom feedback line is the one pixel region (bbox [16,589]-[678,601], measured with PIL ImageChops.difference, same method as evidence/373-focus.json's pixelDiff) that changes between the fixed screenshot and the mutant one; that is the check the mutant reddens, and it is legible from the printed JSON alone without opening the PNG.

revert.confirmedBy: dotnet build src/DungeonFortress.Game/DungeonFortress.Game.csproj after restoring the was line reported 0 warnings, 0 errors; rerunning the before command reproduced controlFeedback "(16,7): 1 of 2 standing here..." and a PNG whose sha256 (840322d4...) matched the pre-mutant capture exactly.
revert.note: The mutant was written, built, run and reverted after the regression-fixed checkpoint was already committed, per Issue #373's own instruction that a mutant only runs after the checkpoint it could otherwise erase is safe.

regressionFoundAndFixed.what: The first version of ApplySelectCellArgument unconditionally overwrote _controlFeedback on every --select-cell call, including cells with zero or one body, with a sentence this Issue invented ("--select-cell (X,Y): focus on creature/raider #N." or "...: nothing stands there."). scripts/verify.ps1's ui stage reddened on tests/golden/ui/stone-t190-loose-no-stockpile.json (and the other two --demo-stone golden frames): they run --demo-stone together with --select-cell on a cell that holds nobody, and depend on an uneventful --select-cell leaving the demo's own feedback sentence ("Demo: DIG marked (25,1)...") in place, exactly as it did before this Issue touched the method.
regressionFoundAndFixed.howFound: The full scripts/verify.ps1 run named in this PR's checkpoint 5 failed on the ui stage with a golden-UI mismatch naming ui.controlFeedback and ui.roster on stone-t190-loose-no-stockpile, stone-t336-in-transit and stone-t950-stockpile-full.
regressionFoundAndFixed.fix: ApplySelectCellArgument now only assigns _controlFeedback when WorldLabels.SelectionHint(state, cell, chosen) returns non-null (bodies.Count >= 2 and a chosen body among them) — the identical rule SelectAt (the click path) already follows for the same reason. A cell with zero or one body is left exactly as untouched as it always was.
regressionFoundAndFixed.consequenceForThisFile: The mutant's "after" feedback text changed from an invented "nothing stands there" sentence to the plain pre-existing brush-picker sentence once the regression fix landed; both before and after captures in this file were re-measured against the regression-fixed build, not against the earlier, since-discarded draft.
